q-277276.name: Question 1
q-277276.problem:
Determine the domain of $f(x)=4\sqrt{7+x}+1.$

The domain is $x\in [${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$).$
q-277276.worked_solution:
The domain of $y=\sqrt{x}$ is

$$
x\ge 0.
$$

To find the domain of $f(x)=4\sqrt{7+x}+1,$ we replace $x$ with $7+x$ in the above inequality. This gives

$$
7+x\ge 0.
$$

Solving this inequality, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}7+x & \ge 0 \\ x & \ge -7.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of $y=f(x)$ is $x\in [-7,\infty ).$

We can also see that this is true from the graph of the function. The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown below.

\begin{aligned}\sqrt{5x+9} & \ge 0 \\ 3\sqrt{5x+9} & \ge 0.\end{aligned}
